base.description: Verified Playwright 1.63 stack checkpoint on canonical main

improvement.name: CDP-confirmed forced MV3 service-worker termination and recovery
improvement.summary: Ferrum can now intentionally terminate the exact loaded MV3 extension service-worker target, independently confirm that original CDP target disappears, then prove a fresh extension event reactivates the worker before the existing full-browser restart proof.
improvement.motivation: Chrome extension service workers may be terminated between events. Ferrum previously proved normal worker behavior and full browser restart, but did not exercise same-browser service-worker destruction and event-driven recovery.

sourceBasis.relevance: Official Chrome testing guidance deliberately closes the extension service-worker target and sends another extension event to verify recovery.
Official lifecycle guidance requires extensions to tolerate service-worker termination and revival by later events.

implementation.mechanism: Create a Chromium CDP session, enumerate Target.getTargets, select exactly one service_worker URL under chrome-extension://<loaded-extension-id>/, call Target.closeTarget, then poll Target.getTargets until the original targetId is absent within the bounded step timeout.
failureBehavior: Fail if the extension ID is unavailable.
Fail if Chromium CDP access is unavailable.
Fail if no matching extension service-worker target exists.
Fail rather than guess when more than one matching service-worker target exists.
Fail if Chrome reports Target.closeTarget success but the original targetId remains present beyond the bounded deadline.
implementation.recoveryFlow: normal ping -> baseline worker diagnostics -> clear popup output -> terminate exact worker -> fresh click -> fresh ok:<extension-id> response -> worker present -> doubled request/response/console diagnostics -> preserve existing full browser restart, post-restart ping, and clean-console checks

supersededProposal.head: 9df36d6e9216af562da2195e57b5c4e5244cb3f1
supersededProposal.failure: Linux and Windows extension smoke observed Chrome accepting the forced close while Playwright did not supply the Worker close diagnostic event used by the first assertion, leaving closedWorkers=0.
supersededProposal.rootCause: Playwright Worker close notification was a weaker signal than authoritative CDP target disappearance for this forced Target.closeTarget operation.
supersededProposal.cleanup: The initial branch also contained an unrelated WebDriver timing edit, so it was closed instead of being patched forward.

candidates.head: 24930af400a17d9671234bc51a4cbf42caaf7e53
candidates.maintenanceFreshness: Active in July 2026; recent upstream work added programmatic library access and continued dump fixes.
candidates.purpose: Trigger Linux/macOS core dumps from process conditions or immediate/manual triggers.
candidates.architecture: ProcDump-compatible process monitor with CLI and newly exposed programmatic library path.
candidates.relevantFerrumCapability: Failure-only native process crash capture before teardown.
candidates.harvest: Condition-triggered or immediate dump creation with process identity preserved.
candidates.integrationMode: Optional subprocess or library-backed crash-capture adapter, never a mandatory dependency.
candidates.expectedBenefit: Actionable native crash artifacts for desktop/process targets when logs end at a hard crash.
candidates.requiredDependencies: Supported Linux/macOS host and ProcDump binary/library; dump storage budget.
candidates.platformCoverage: Linux and macOS upstream focus; Windows already has native ProcDump separately but was not evaluated as the same integration this pass.
candidates.compatibilityRisks: Host permissions, core-dump policy, disk usage, attaching to short-lived processes.
candidates.upstreamIssues: No blocking upstream issue identified in this pass; integration must explicitly handle ptrace/core restrictions.
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: Sysinternals-compatible project with active upstream maintenance and current programmatic-access work.
candidates.smallestExperiment: Run a tiny native crash fixture under Ferrum process supervision, trigger/collect one dump, verify process/build identity, artifact size and cleanup.
candidates.acceptanceTest: Crash path produces one bounded dump plus structured metadata with no normal-success overhead or loss of existing logs/evidence.
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: Run after the MV3 merge when a crash fixture and host core-dump capability can be exercised end-to-end.

candidates.head: 4adf5555b2ab844f23c52982fc202357ff882695
candidates.purpose: Parse, process and stackwalk minidump files.
candidates.architecture: Rust crates plus minidump-stackwalk CLI; structured JSON output is a supported analysis surface.
candidates.relevantFerrumCapability: Convert raw Chromium/Electron/native minidumps into machine-readable crash reason/thread/stack evidence.
candidates.harvest: Local deterministic stackwalk/JSON sidecar while retaining raw dump bytes.
candidates.integrationMode: Optional analysis sidecar or subprocess adapter after a dump exists.
candidates.expectedBenefit: Agents can classify crashes without manually opening a debugger or losing the original dump.
candidates.requiredDependencies: rust-minidump CLI/binary or library; optional symbols for deeper stacks.
candidates.platformCoverage: Cross-platform minidump analysis; actual dump acquisition remains target-specific.
candidates.compatibilityRisks: Symbol availability, analysis cost on very large dumps, tool version pinning.
candidates.upstreamIssues: No blocker identified; symbol resolution must remain optional and explicit.
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: Project recommends minidump-processor or minidump-stackwalk and exposes JSON suitable for automation.
candidates.smallestExperiment: Feed a release-pinned known minidump fixture through stackwalk JSON and store summary plus raw dump in Ferrum evidence.
candidates.acceptanceTest: Stable structured crash summary is generated offline with bounded time/size, and raw dump remains intact and hashable.
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: Pair with the first ProcDump/Crashpad dump acquisition experiment.

candidates.head: 5ebcc30bef4af60d6e28f012dd8bf7b99b8b0acf
candidates.maintenanceFreshness: Maintained through July 2026; release 3.6 shipped in March 2026.
candidates.purpose: Linux process isolation using namespaces, resource limits and seccomp-bpf.
candidates.architecture: Standalone supervisor with ONCE/EXECVE/RERUN/LISTEN modes, namespace isolation, filesystem mounts, cgroups and Kafel seccomp policies.
candidates.relevantFerrumCapability: Optional isolated process/service target execution with deterministic cleanup and resource constraints.
candidates.harvest: Reusable isolation profile contract around Ferrum process targets, not one-off shell wrappers.
candidates.integrationMode: Optional Linux process adapter/profile behind existing lifecycle and evidence contracts.
candidates.expectedBenefit: Safer disposable test processes, better containment of leaks and deterministic resource ceilings.
candidates.requiredDependencies: Linux kernel namespace/seccomp/cgroup capabilities and nsjail binary.
candidates.compatibilityRisks: Host kernel/user-namespace policy, filesystem/network access differences, required capabilities in CI/container hosts.
candidates.upstreamIssues: No blocking issue identified; host policy variability is the main integration risk.
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: Upstream exposes explicit limits, mount policies, network isolation and repeated-execution modes useful for fuzz/test workloads.
candidates.smallestExperiment: Run the same deterministic Ferrum process fixture isolated and unisolated, then compare output, evidence, cleanup, startup cost and resource behavior.
candidates.acceptanceTest: Identical functional result and evidence with improved containment, explicit unsupported-host errors, and no hidden permissions or data loss.
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: After crash capture experiment or when a project needs untrusted/local process isolation.

candidates.head: 99ff0a2bf4becb17265d0e07ecabe8a564ea2c6c
candidates.maintenanceFreshness: Active through August 2026; latest release line is compatible with Ferrum's Node 24 baseline.

candidates.architecture: Node library controlling Docker-compatible runtimes with wait strategies, cleanup and container lifecycle abstractions.
candidates.relevantFerrumCapability: Reusable API/service test fixtures for databases, queues and dependent services.
candidates.harvest: Capability-detected disposable service fixture provider with health, identity and cleanup evidence.
candidates.integrationMode: Optional fixture adapter, never a requirement for ordinary Ferrum tests.
candidates.expectedBenefit: Real service integration testing without hand-managed daemon setup or leaked test services.

candidates.platformCoverage: Hosts with a supported Docker-compatible runtime; exact engine/OS must be capability-checked.

candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: Mature integration-test ecosystem; current versions include healthcheck and cleanup work relevant to deterministic service fixtures.
candidates.smallestExperiment: Launch one tiny HTTP or data-service fixture, wait for health, interact through Ferrum, induce one failure, restart if applicable and verify cleanup.

candidates.head: 2f55bae38468d0c50cf5df87b1e481e882b63acb
candidates.maintenanceFreshness: Maintained in 2026 with current security-oriented release activity.
candidates.purpose: Unprivileged Linux sandboxing using namespaces and explicit filesystem/process setup.
candidates.architecture: Small sandbox setup binary often used as a lower-level isolation primitive.
candidates.relevantFerrumCapability: Alternative lightweight Linux process isolation backend.
candidates.harvest: Compare compatibility/startup footprint against nsjail for ordinary process fixtures.
candidates.integrationMode: WATCH first; optional adapter only if it outperforms nsjail for Ferrum workloads.
candidates.expectedBenefit: Potentially lighter process isolation while preserving explicit mounts and namespace boundaries.
candidates.compatibilityRisks: Security posture depends heavily on invocation; upstream now has an explicit mode that callers must not use when relying on it as a security boundary.
candidates.upstreamIssues: No single blocker identified; configuration correctness is the primary risk.
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: Widely used sandbox primitive with active 2026 maintenance.
candidates.smallestExperiment: Run the same deterministic process fixture used for nsjail and compare compatibility, setup latency and evidence behavior.
candidates.acceptanceTest: At least parity with nsjail experiment on functionality/evidence and a measurable simplicity or performance advantage before adoption.
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: Re-evaluate after nsjail benchmark or if a Ferrum target needs a smaller rootless sandbox primitive.

candidates.head: ae978c33ba45a98a24c41079d5c2c27a34eaee85
candidates.maintenanceFreshness: Current release activity in May 2026 and repository updates in April 2026.
candidates.purpose: Capture Linux system-call/process activity with ProcMon-style filters and persisted output.
candidates.architecture: eBPF-based process monitor with CLI/headless operation and database output.
candidates.relevantFerrumCapability: Failure-only process diagnostics when stdout/stderr do not reveal missing file/socket/process causes.
candidates.harvest: Attach filtered diagnostics to a failing process target while keeping normal successful runs cheap.
candidates.expectedBenefit: Faster root-cause classification for file/network/process failures.
candidates.requiredDependencies: Linux eBPF-capable host, ProcMon binary and necessary permissions.
candidates.compatibilityRisks: Kernel/eBPF support, elevated permissions, potentially large evidence databases.
candidates.upstreamIssues: No blocker identified; privilege and output-volume constraints require a strict Ferrum budget.
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: Sysinternals-style diagnostic tool with PID/syscall filtering and headless persisted output.
candidates.smallestExperiment: Run a fixture that fails on a missing file or connection and capture only the relevant process/syscall subset.
candidates.acceptanceTest: Failure root cause becomes materially clearer with bounded artifact size and negligible success-path cost.
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: Compare against strace on the first difficult Linux process failure.

candidates.head: c41af8463a9d61c7b750432cb8cd0fbf08a4e782
candidates.purpose: High-level dynamic tracing over eBPF probes.
candidates.architecture: Tracing language/runtime compiling probes to eBPF with kernel/user process observability.
candidates.relevantFerrumCapability: Advanced Linux diagnostics for races, process lifecycle and kernel/user interactions.
candidates.harvest: Targeted diagnostics only where simpler logs/strace/ProcMon are insufficient.
candidates.integrationMode: WATCH; optional expert diagnostic adapter at most.
candidates.expectedBenefit: Deep observability for otherwise opaque timing and kernel interaction failures.
candidates.requiredDependencies: Compatible Linux kernel, bpftrace tooling and privileges/capabilities.

candidates.upstreamIssues: No blocker identified; complexity itself makes this inappropriate as a default path.
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: Actively maintained tracing ecosystem with broad probe support.
candidates.smallestExperiment: Only after a real failure resists simpler diagnostics, capture one bounded process-lifecycle probe set.
candidates.acceptanceTest: Adds uniquely actionable evidence not available from simpler tools with a strict overhead and output budget.
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: A real Ferrum process/runtime failure that cannot be diagnosed with existing logs plus strace/ProcMon.

candidates.head: 48b459d7aed33d3b47c8c2c3daff12716b95c2d5

candidates.relevantFerrumCapability: Simple failure-only syscall evidence for process/service targets.

candidates.head: c205f555004b253f7ca624d1d2c6629ab26c54ff
candidates.maintenanceFreshness: Current repository work in 2026 includes a persistent shell execution service.
candidates.purpose: Agent-oriented shell execution utilities including a persistent pre-configured shell server/client.
candidates.architecture: Local Unix-domain-socket process server forwarding stdio and signals into a persistent shell environment.
candidates.relevantFerrumCapability: Reduce repeated shell/environment setup for agent-driven process tests.
candidates.harvest: Persistent environment/session pattern, process-group signal forwarding and restricted local socket permissions.
candidates.integrationMode: TRANSPLANT-IDEA only; Ferrum-native session contract preferred over direct dependency.
candidates.expectedBenefit: Fewer setup/tool round trips for repeated CLI/process workflows while keeping one known environment identity.
candidates.requiredDependencies: Unix-style local process/socket environment for the upstream implementation pattern.
candidates.platformCoverage: Current upstream implementation is Unix-oriented; Ferrum would need its own cross-platform abstraction.
candidates.compatibilityRisks: The upstream shell server is explicitly not a security boundary; persistence can retain unintended mutable state.
candidates.upstreamIssues: Security/isolation filtering is intentionally outside the upstream server's current scope.
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: Recent upstream work directly targets persistent shell startup/setup amortization for agents.
candidates.smallestExperiment: Measure repeated deterministic CLI tasks in a persistent Ferrum process session versus fresh process setup using the same environment and evidence.
candidates.acceptanceTest: Lower setup time/tool calls with identical outputs, explicit state identity/reset and no weakened isolation claims.
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: After measuring repeated process setup as a real Ferrum bottleneck.

candidates.head: a6aeffea485db5629c64dc3805d2764dbc7a77b2
candidates.maintenanceFreshness: Active on August 17, 2026, including current native minidump/crash-handler analysis fixes.
candidates.purpose: Native crash/error reporting SDK for C/C++ applications.
candidates.architecture: Embedded native SDK with crash backends and reporting/transport integration.
candidates.relevantFerrumCapability: Reference architecture for native crash capture, but not a good direct fit for Ferrum's provider-neutral local evidence model.
candidates.harvest: Review native crash-handler hardening patterns only.
candidates.integrationMode: Do not add as a Ferrum dependency at this time.
candidates.expectedBenefit: Limited for Ferrum compared with local dump capture plus independent analysis.
candidates.requiredDependencies: Native SDK integration and application/build changes, which would violate Ferrum's goal of testing arbitrary apps without invasive instrumentation.
candidates.compatibilityRisks: Invasive app instrumentation, transport/reporting semantics, native build churn and possible conflict with the application's existing crash handler.
candidates.upstreamIssues: Standalone usage is documented upstream as experimental/best-effort rather than the preferred product integration path.
candidates.benchmarkOrProductionEvidence: Mature Sentry ecosystem, but direct embedding does not match Ferrum's non-invasive local-evidence requirement.
candidates.smallestExperiment: None unless a future project already embeds sentry-native and Ferrum merely needs to collect its existing local artifacts.
candidates.acceptanceTest: Reconsider only if it adds unique non-invasive evidence unavailable from ProcDump/Crashpad plus rust-minidump.
candidates.nextReviewTrigger: A tested application already uses sentry-native and exposes useful local crash artifacts Ferrum can consume without instrumentation.

challengePass.reason: The MV3 lifecycle improvement already required a full cross-platform gate and one failure-driven redesign. Crash capture and isolation candidates are promising, but none had a same-workload baseline plus real-runtime fixture executed in this pass. Shipping one without that proof would violate the proven-improvement gate.
nextExperiments: ProcDump-for-Linux crash fixture plus rust-minidump JSON analysis, preserving raw dump and build/runtime identity.
nsjail isolated process fixture compared against the same unisolated process workload for correctness, evidence, cleanup and startup cost.
strace bounded failure-only diagnostics on a deliberately missing-file or connection fixture; compare with ProcMon only if simpler tracing is insufficient.
Testcontainers Node disposable service fixture after crash/isolation contracts are stable.

researchCursorNext: crash-dump acquisition and structured minidump analysis; then Linux process isolation; then disposable service/API fixtures and bounded failure-only syscall diagnostics
guardrails: No reduced target coverage, skipped runtime proof, quality/fidelity loss, diagnostic loss, item/data caps, viewport-only shortcuts, stale caching or weaker tests.
New crash/isolation/service adapters remain optional and additive until real-runtime parity plus measurable value is proven.
Raw evidence must remain available even when structured summaries are added.
Failure-only diagnostics must have explicit size/time budgets and must not add material success-path overhead.
Existing Linux, Windows, browser matrix, MV3 restart, Spaces, Workbench, packaged desktop, Lightpanda, WebDriver Grid, MCP and Android/Appium paths remain acceptance gates according to affected risk.

publication.verification: Canonical payload is hashed locally before GitHub publication. GitHub file is re-read. The same payload and hash are appended to the Ferrum Drive checkpoint, then the full Drive document is re-read/exported and independently hashed.
